newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RESEARCH ALERT-Manila shares down but not for long.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Manila shares down but not for long.

text.p: The Philippine stock market, one of the world's worst performers this year, will eventually come back into favour but investors need to be very selective over the short term, the research head at Socgen-Crosby UBP Securities said on Wednesday.
"We are quite positive on this market long-term, but expect it to be choppy in the short-term," Raphael Manalaysay told reporters.
"Bottom-up (over the next 12-18 months) is the best approach and be very, very selective," he added.
For asset allocation, the company was slightly underweight on the Philippines in the next three months, moving to a little overweight over the next 12 months.
Manalaysay predicted the index, which has been hammered in recent weeks by fears over a property glut and disappointing first quarter earnings, would end the year around 2,700.
That compares to 2,796 at the close on Wednesday.
But by the end of next year, it should have reached 3,381, up almost 50 percent with multiples of 14 times compared with 16.5 times in 1997.
Investors should focus on mergers and acquistions, company downsizing, and firms concentrating on their core activities.
Currency risks partly from current account imbalances and political uncertainties running up to next year's presidential election could temper the upward momentum.
He doubted the property market, fears over whose fate have been dominating the market, would collapse but warned that there would be a correction and gluts are likely in certain segments.
But overall the real estate market should be healthy, especially in the main financial districts of the capital.

On the plus side, companies are doing well with growing competition, valuations are more reasonable, earnings growth is likely to be strong and most of the bad news has already been factored in the market, he said.
